examples.en: The police interrogated the suspect all night.
The scene where the lawyer questions the witness was striking.

examples.ko: 검사는 피고인을 신문하고 나서 의견을 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The prosecutor gave his opinion after questioning the defendant.

examples.ko: 형사가 내일 사건 관계자를 신문할 거예요.
examples.en: The detective will question the people involved in the case tomorrow.

examples.ko: 그 형사가 신문한 사람은 모두 열 명이에요.
examples.en: The detective questioned ten people in all.
Why do you keep asking me questions like you are interrogating me?

explain: 법정이나 수사처럼 공식적인 자리에서 캐묻는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서는 '물어보다', 따지듯 계속 묻는 건 '캐묻다'를 써요. 종이 '신문'과 소리가 같아서 '증인을 신문하다'처럼 함께 쓰는 말로 구분해요.
explain_en: This is a stiff word for formal questioning in courts or police investigations. In daily life use '물어보다', and for pressing someone with questions use '캐묻다'. It sounds the same as '신문' (newspaper), so tell them apart by the words around it, as in '증인을 신문하다'.

en: be detached; be cut off; be isolated

examples.ko: 정책이 현실과 유리되면 아무도 따르지 않아요.
examples.en: If a policy is detached from reality, nobody follows it.

examples.ko: 이 이론은 현장과 유리되어 있어서 쓸모가 적어요.
examples.en: This theory is cut off from the field, so it is not very useful.

examples.ko: 오래 혼자 지내다 보니 세상과 유리된 느낌이에요.
examples.en: After being alone for so long, I feel cut off from the world.

examples.ko: 학생들의 생각과 유리된 수업은 재미가 없어요.
examples.en: A class disconnected from what students think is boring.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 결정은 직원들의 의견과 유리됐어요.
examples.en: The company's decision was out of touch with the employees' opinions.

examples.ko: 현실과 유리되지 않도록 뉴스를 매일 봐요.
examples.en: I watch the news every day so I do not lose touch with reality.

explain: '현실과 유리되다', '대중과 유리되다'처럼 '~과/와' 앞에 떨어져 있는 대상을 붙여 써요. 물건이 아니라 생각, 정책, 사람이 현실이나 현장에서 멀어졌을 때 쓰고 뉴스와 글에서 자주 보여요. 창문 '유리'와는 관계가 없어요.
explain_en: Put the thing that someone is cut off from before '~과/와', as in '현실과 유리되다' or '대중과 유리되다'. It is used for ideas, policies and people drifting away from reality or the field, not for physical objects, and it appears mostly in news and writing. It has nothing to do with '유리' (glass).

examples.en: This year was declared the 'Year of Reading'.
Once a state of emergency was declared, the schools closed.
The start of the tournament was declared and the players walked in.
They set the day independence was declared as a commemorative day.

examples.ko: 내일 휴업이 선언될 거라는 소문이 돌아요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that a shutdown will be declared tomorrow.

examples.ko: 파업이 선언되었지만 회사는 아직 답이 없어요.
examples.en: A strike has been declared, but the company has not responded yet.

explain: '선언하다'는 사람이 직접 공표하는 것이고, '선언되다'는 공식 선언이 이루어진 결과를 말해요. '독립이', '비상사태가', '휴업이' 선언되다처럼 큰 공식 사건에 써요. 개인의 다짐은 '선언하다'나 '말하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '선언하다' is when someone announces something; '선언되다' describes the result once an official declaration has been made. It fits big public events like '독립이', '비상사태가', '휴업이' 선언되다. For personal resolutions, '선언하다' or '말하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: This building was designed to withstand earthquakes.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 아이들도 쉽게 쓸 수 있게 설계되었어요.
examples.en: This app is designed so that even children can use it easily.

examples.ko: 설계된 대로 공사하면 석 달쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: If we build it as designed, it will take about three months.
I wonder how the new library will be designed.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 허리를 편하게 하려고 설계되어서 오래 앉아도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: This chair is designed to be easy on the back, so sitting long is fine.

examples.ko: 처음부터 잘 설계되지 않은 시스템은 고치기 어려워요.
examples.en: A system that was not well designed from the start is hard to fix.

explain: 건물, 기계, 프로그램, 제도처럼 목적을 생각해서 미리 짜 놓은 것에 써요. '만들어지다'는 완성된 결과에, '설계되다'는 만들기 전의 구조와 의도에 초점이 있어요. '~도록/~게 설계되다' 형태가 가장 흔해요.
explain_en: Use it for things whose structure was planned in advance with a purpose: buildings, machines, programs, systems. '만들어지다' focuses on the finished result, while '설계되다' focuses on the plan and intent behind it. The most common pattern is '~도록/~게 설계되다'.

examples.en: The rain has been going on for three days now.
The heat will last until next week.

examples.ko: 이 약의 효과는 한 달쯤 지속돼요.
examples.en: The effect of this medicine lasts about a month.

examples.ko: 지속되는 소음 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I could not sleep because of the constant noise.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 대화는 오래 지속되지 못했어요.
examples.en: The talks between the two countries did not last long.

examples.ko: 좋은 관계가 지속되려면 서로 노력해야 해요.
examples.en: For a good relationship to last, both people have to make an effort.

explain: '계속되다'와 비슷하지만 '지속되다'는 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 '계속되다'가 더 자연스러워요. 비, 더위, 효과, 관계처럼 시간이 이어지는 것에 쓰고 '지속 가능한'처럼 앞에 붙는 말도 많아요.
explain_en: It is close to '계속되다', but '지속되다' appears more in news and writing, while '계속되다' is more natural in speech. It fits things that run over time, like rain, heat, effects and relationships, and '지속' also appears in set phrases such as '지속 가능한' (sustainable).

examples.en: This exercise keeps the effect going for a long time.

examples.ko: 좋은 습관을 지속시키려면 매일 조금씩 하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: To keep a good habit going, it is best to do a little every day.

examples.ko: 회사는 이 서비스를 앞으로도 지속시킬 계획이에요.
examples.en: The company plans to keep this service running in the future too.

examples.ko: 그는 어려운 상황에서도 좋은 성적을 지속시켰어요.
examples.en: He kept his good grades going even in a hard situation.
Keeping people's interest going is the hardest part.
I am sorry I could not keep that enthusiasm going.

explain: '계속하다'는 하던 일을 이어서 하는 것이고, '지속시키다'는 상태나 효과가 끊기지 않게 하는 쪽이에요. 목적어로 '효과, 관계, 관심, 서비스'처럼 상태를 나타내는 말이 와요. 말할 때는 '유지하다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: '계속하다' means to carry on doing something, while '지속시키다' is about making a state or effect not break off. Its objects are state-like nouns such as '효과', '관계', '관심', '서비스'. In speech, '유지하다' is more common.

examples.ko: 파일을 저장하면 새 폴더가 자동으로 생성돼요.
examples.en: When you save the file, a new folder is created automatically.
This account was created yesterday afternoon.

examples.ko: 별은 가스와 먼지가 모여 생성되었다고 해요.
examples.en: They say stars were formed when gas and dust gathered together.
Please write down the newly generated password.

examples.ko: 문서가 생성되는 데 몇 초가 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a few seconds for the document to be generated.

examples.ko: 오류가 생성되지 않도록 순서대로 눌러 주세요.
examples.en: Please press them in order so that no error is generated.

explain: 컴퓨터와 과학 분야에서 특히 자주 써요. '파일이 생성되다', '계정이 생성되다'처럼 시스템이 자동으로 만들 때 어울려요. 사람이 손으로 만드는 건 '만들다'를 써요. '생성하다'가 능동, '생성되다'가 피동이에요.
explain_en: Common in computing and science. It fits cases where a system produces something automatically, as in '파일이 생성되다' or '계정이 생성되다'. For things people make by hand, use '만들다'. '생성하다' is active and '생성되다' is passive.

examples.en: This program generates reports automatically.
I created a new account first.

examples.ko: 사진 없이 그림을 생성하는 기술이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Technology that generates pictures without photos is increasing.
After you generate the password, be sure to save it.

examples.ko: 파일을 생성할 때 이름을 꼭 입력해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to enter a name when you create a file.
If you generate the data all at once, the computer slows down.

explain: 주로 컴퓨터나 기술 이야기에서 써요. 사람이 직접 하나를 만드는 일은 '만들다', 프로그램이 새로 내놓는 일은 '생성하다'가 잘 맞아요. 주로 '파일, 계정, 보고서, 이미지' 같은 말과 함께 쓰여요.
explain_en: Mostly used when talking about computers and technology. When a person makes one thing, use '만들다'; when a program produces something new, '생성하다' fits well. It is usually paired with words like '파일', '계정', '보고서', '이미지'.

examples.en: Words are combined and new words are formed.
Consonants and vowels are put together to make a letter.

examples.ko: 여러 재료가 조합된 샌드위치가 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: The sandwich that combines several ingredients is very popular.

examples.ko: 색깔이 어떻게 조합되느냐에 따라 느낌이 달라요.
examples.en: The feel changes depending on how the colors are combined.

examples.ko: 숫자 네 개가 조합되면 비밀번호가 돼요.
examples.en: When four numbers are put together, they make a password.

examples.ko: 좋은 팀은 서로 다른 장점이 잘 조합되어 있어요.
examples.en: In a good team, different strengths are well combined.

explain: '조합하다'는 사람이 짜 맞추는 쪽이고, '조합되다'는 여럿이 합쳐져 하나가 된 결과를 말해요. 글자, 색, 재료, 숫자처럼 부분이 여러 개일 때 써요. 그냥 섞이는 '섞이다'보다 짜임새가 있는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '조합하다' is when a person puts parts together; '조합되다' describes the result of several parts forming one whole. Use it when there are several components, such as letters, colors, ingredients or numbers. Compared with '섞이다' (to mix), it feels more structured.

examples.en: If your skin is exposed to the sun for a long time, it gets damaged.
Personal information was exposed on the internet and caused a problem.

examples.ko: 아이가 너무 일찍 스마트폰에 노출되지 않게 해요.
examples.en: I make sure my child is not exposed to smartphones too early.
I was very worried that the secret would be exposed.
They blurred the faces that were visible on camera.
His weakness was exposed, but he did not panic.

explain: '~에 노출되다'는 햇빛, 위험, 소음, 정보처럼 좋지 않은 것에 그대로 닿는 상황에 자주 써요. 비밀이나 약점은 '드러나다'도 가능한데, '노출되다'는 뉴스에서 더 딱딱하게 들려요. 사진의 밝기를 말하는 '노출'도 같은 단어예요.
explain_en: '~에 노출되다' is often used for being left open to something unwelcome, like sunlight, danger, noise or information. For secrets and weaknesses '드러나다' also works, but '노출되다' sounds more formal, like in news. The '노출' in photography (exposure) is the same word.

examples.en: The screen suddenly switches to a different scene.
This semester's classes were switched to online.

examples.ko: 회의 분위기가 밝게 전환되자 모두 웃었어요.
examples.en: Once the mood of the meeting turned brighter, everyone laughed.
The pace of the switch to electric cars is getting faster.
I was worried the situation would turn against us.

examples.ko: 휴대폰이 무음 모드로 전환된 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I did not know the phone had switched to silent mode.

explain: 상태, 방식, 방향이 다른 것으로 바뀔 때 써요. '온라인으로 전환되다', '분위기가 전환되다'처럼 말해요. '바뀌다'보다 딱딱하고 큰 변화에 어울려요. 기분을 바꾼다는 '기분 전환'도 같은 한자어예요.
explain_en: Use it when a state, method or direction changes into another, as in '온라인으로 전환되다' or '분위기가 전환되다'. It is more formal than '바뀌다' and fits bigger changes. '기분 전환' (a change of mood) uses the same word.

en: change; switch over; shift (something) on purpose

examples.en: The teacher steered the topic in another direction.

examples.ko: 회사는 종이 문서를 전자 문서로 전환시켜요.
examples.en: The company converts paper documents into electronic ones.
I opened the window to change the mood.
They built a device that converts heat into electricity.
If you switch your way of thinking, the problem gets easy to solve.
They plan to shift the market toward online.

explain: '전환하다'와 거의 같아서 보통은 '전환하다'를 더 많이 써요. '전환시키다'는 누군가가 일부러 방향을 돌린다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 화제, 분위기, 방식 같은 말과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '전환하다', which people use more often. '전환시키다' has a stronger sense that someone deliberately turns things around. It goes with words like '화제', '분위기', '방식'.

examples.ko: 저는 학교에서 아이 취급당하는 게 싫어요.
examples.en: I do not like being treated like a child at school.
He was treated like luggage, not like a guest.
I'm an adult, but being treated like a little kid made me feel bad.

examples.ko: 문제아로 취급당하지 않으려고 더 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: I worked harder so I would not be treated as a troublemaker.
I am always treated like the youngest, so it upsets me.
A person must not be treated like an object.

explain: '아이 취급당하다'처럼 앞에 '~ 취급'이 붙고, 보통 불만이나 억울함이 담겨요. 좋은 대접을 받을 때는 '대우받다'를 써요. '취급받다'도 비슷하지만 '당하다'가 더 억울한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It appears as '~ 취급당하다', as in '아이 취급당하다', and usually carries a complaint or sense of unfairness. For good treatment, use '대우받다'. '취급받다' is similar, but '당하다' sounds more resentful.

examples.en: Imported fruit is also handled at this market.
That was treated as a simple mistake.
Dangerous items must be handled with care.

examples.ko: 지각 세 번은 결석 한 번으로 취급된다고 해요.
examples.en: They say three late arrivals are counted as one absence.

examples.ko: 한 번 쓴 제품은 중고로 취급되니까 값이 내려가요.
examples.en: A used product is treated as secondhand, so its price drops.

examples.ko: 중고 책은 새 책과 같은 값으로 취급되지 않아요.
examples.en: Used books are not treated at the same price as new books.

explain: 사람보다는 일, 물건, 상품이 어떻게 다뤄지는지에 써요. '중고로 취급되다', '이 가게에서 취급되다'처럼 말해요. 사람이 억울하게 대접받는 건 '취급당하다'예요. 가게 안내문의 '취급 품목'이라는 말도 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used for how things, jobs or products are handled rather than for people, as in '중고로 취급되다' or '이 가게에서 취급되다'. When a person is treated unfairly, use '취급당하다'. You also often see '취급 품목' (items handled) on store notices.

en: be released (film); be opened; be unsealed

examples.en: That movie will be released next week.

examples.ko: 개봉된 지 일주일 만에 백만 명이 봤어요.
examples.en: A million people saw it within a week of its release.

examples.ko: 포장이 이미 개봉되어 있어서 환불이 안 돼요.
examples.en: The package has already been opened, so a refund is not possible.

examples.ko: 새 영화가 개봉되는 날 친구와 극장에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I will go to the theater with a friend on the day the new film opens.
I watched the trailer before the film was released.
I rewatched a movie that was released last year.

explain: 영화가 처음 극장에서 상영될 때 주로 '개봉되다'를 써요. 이미 한 번 나온 영화를 다시 올리면 '재개봉'이라고 해요. 포장을 연다는 뜻은 쇼핑에서 '개봉 상품', '미개봉'으로 자주 써요. 상자나 편지를 여는 일은 '열다', '뜯다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Mostly used when a film first opens in theaters. A film shown again is called '재개봉'. In shopping, the sense of opening a package shows up in '개봉 상품' (opened item) and '미개봉' (unopened). For opening a box or letter in speech, '열다' or '뜯다' is more natural.

en: be included (in a book or album)

examples.en: This poem is included in the textbook.
That song was included on the new album.

examples.ko: 사전에 수록된 단어는 십만 개가 넘어요.
examples.en: The dictionary has more than a hundred thousand entries.

examples.ko: 이 책에는 유명한 작가의 글이 열 편 수록돼 있어요.
examples.en: This book contains ten pieces by famous writers.

examples.ko: 제 사진이 다음 호 잡지에 수록될 예정이에요.
examples.en: My photo is scheduled to appear in the next issue of the magazine.

examples.ko: 수록되지 않은 단어는 따로 찾아봐야 해요.
examples.en: Words that are not included have to be looked up separately.

explain: 책, 앨범, 사전처럼 여러 항목을 모은 곳에 글, 곡, 단어가 담길 때 써요. '~에 수록되다'가 기본 형태예요. 말할 때는 '실리다', '들어 있다'가 더 쉬워요.
explain_en: Use it when a piece of writing, a song or a word is gathered into a collection such as a book, album or dictionary. The basic pattern is '~에 수록되다'. In speech, '실리다' or '들어 있다' is easier.

en: far off; remote (in time or likelihood)

examples.en: Unification still seems a long way off.
Peace feels far away, but I do not give up.
It is still a long way off for our team to win the championship.

examples.ko: 해결이 요원할 줄 알았는데 생각보다 빨랐어요.
examples.en: I thought a solution was far off, but it came sooner than expected.
A dream that once seemed out of reach became reality.

examples.ko: 집을 사는 일은 지금 월급으로는 요원하죠.
examples.en: Buying a house is out of reach on my current salary.

explain: 시간이나 가능성이 아주 멀리 있어서 이루기 어려울 때 써요. '통일이 요원하다', '성공이 요원하다'처럼 목표나 희망에 붙여요. 거리가 먼 건 '멀다'를 써요. 주로 뉴스나 글에서 보여요.
explain_en: Use it when something is so far away in time or likelihood that it is hard to achieve, as in '통일이 요원하다' or '성공이 요원하다'. Physical distance is '멀다'. It is a stiff word found in news and writing.
